Growing faith amid suffering leads into hope for relief and prayer for good work

Verses 6–10 promise relief at the Lord’s revealing, which is still future. Verse 11 says what the writers ask for the time between. “To this end” ties the prayer to that day. They ask God to count the readers worthy of their calling. They ask him to complete every good desire and work of faith with power. The work is the readers’, and the power is God’s. Verse 12 gives the aim: the name of Jesus glorified in them.
Claims that the day has arrived must answer the instruction already received

Verse 2 names three ways a false report could come: spirit, word, or letter. Any of them might claim the writers’ authority. Verse 5 reminds them that Paul told them these things in person. Verse 15 gives the test that follows. They are to hold what the writers taught, by word or by letter. A new claim is measured against that teaching. Verse 3:17 adds a safeguard: Paul’s own handwriting marks every letter.
Refusal of work calls for correction that still recognizes a brother

Verse 14 tells them to note a disobedient person and keep away. The stated aim is that he be ashamed. Verse 15 limits how far that goes. He is not to be counted an enemy. He is to be admonished, and the word used for him is still “brother.” Verse 6 used the same word at the start of the instruction. The distance is meant to correct him, not to disown him.
